run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T11:41:47Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by frontend-proxy answering HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout whenever its upstream reply exceeds the proxy's ~15 s timeout. In the sampled trace f18dd56ad5afb108674a31c6c7770ed1 the proxy ingress span 4c3095911506c158 lasted 15.00 s and its child 'router frontend egress' span 2dc03d0c22271621 to frontend lasted 15.00 s, while the frontend request underneath (POST /api/checkout, 89.09 s) waited on checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (89.08 s), whose 'orders publish' span hung 88.87 s with otel.status_description 'circuit breaker is open'. checkout's logs show repeated 'kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open' plus a 30 s 'read tcp 100.96.1.134:53048->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout' against the kafka Service ClusterIP, and both kafka pods log a STALE_BROKER_EPOCH / 'Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10' loop, so kafka could not serve the producer. That checkout->kafka path was already failing at the alert start (checkout logs from 11:49:32) and its steady ~0.38-0.49/s checkout error rate tracks the proxy's baseline 0.40-0.47/s. A second, later contributor is the frontend 'GET /api/data' / 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' error stream (0.25-0.72/s from the 12:01:47 bucket), which coincides with ad's container being OOMKilled (exit 137) and restarted at 11:59:28 and already back at ~99% of its 450Mi limit. The deepest cause of kafka's instability (two broker replicas sharing one KRaft voter/node id, versus an injected network fault evidenced by PodNetworkChaos objects) remains unresolved because the chaos specs and pre-11:55 kafka logs could not be read.

Rejected: the frontend-proxy pod itself failing or restarting. frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-59tsm is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, and the sampled 504 spans show the full 15 s spent inside the proxy's child 'router frontend egress' call to frontend, i.e. an upstream timeout rather than a proxy fault.

Rejected: kafka Service or endpoint misconfiguration. Service kafka (ClusterIP 100.71.78.255) selects opentelemetry.io/name=kafka and its endpoints list both broker pod IPs 100.96.2.21 and 100.96.4.61 with ports 9092/9093, so the address that timed out was a correctly populated Service.

Leading explanation for the kafka side: the KRaft control plane cannot stabilise because the Deployment runs 2 broker replicas while the only configured voter is 1@kafka:9093 (a name that load-balances to either pod) and both pods log controller id=1; the resulting conflicting broker-1 registrations would explain 'Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10' and the STALE_BROKER_EPOCH retry loop, leaving the brokers unable to serve checkout's produce requests.

Alternative unresolved explanation for the same symptom: a network fault between the checkout pod and the kafka pods. PodNetworkChaos objects exist and were repeatedly updated for checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l and both kafka pods during the window, and checkout's failure includes a 30 s TCP read timeout ('i/o timeout') to the kafka Service IP; the chaos specs could not be read, so target, direction and duration are unverified.

The additional frontend 'GET /api/data' / 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' errors (and the matching proxy 5xx) are attributable to ad becoming unavailable: ad's container was OOMKilled and restarted at 11:59:28, inside the first bucket showing those errors, and the replacement container is already near its 450Mi limit. No trace exists after 11:59:21 to confirm the error text or status, and ad's own error spans appear only later (flagd ResolveBoolean 0.131/s in the bucket ending 12:11:47).

Determine whether the PodNetworkChaos objects on checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l and the two kafka pods are the intended fault and remove or expire them, and independently reconcile the kafka Deployment with its KRaft configuration (2 replicas versus a single voter 1@kafka:9093, duplicated broker/controller identity) so broker registrations stop conflicting.

Raise the ad container's 450Mi memory limit (or lower its memory use): it was OOMKilled at 11:59:28 and the replacement container already reached ~99% of the limit, so another OOM-driven spike on /api/data is likely.
